 Shopping Our Readers Can't Get Enough Of These K-Beauty Products — And For Good Reason
 Calming recovery creams, sunscreens that feel like magic, dark spot-erasers and more innovative goodness.
 By   Tessa Flores Senior shopping writer
 Oct 31, 2026, 06:00 AM EDT Leave a Comment Amazon K-beauty products that HuffPost readers love. History would prove that our reporting has long endorsed K-beauty products, from the formulas we personally use every day to the viral hits that are sweeping social media. 
 It’s a category that’s impossible to ignore — many consider Korean formulas to be the height of beauty innovation , and it’s no secret that these products are often affordably priced.
 Advertisement 
 Though our coverage dates back several years, when we were waxing poetic about the Cosrx snail mucin serum or mind-blowing sunscreens that don’t leave even a hint of a white cast, we’ve seen a surge in reader interest in the last year.
 You can see for yourself the 13 K-beauty products that HuffPost shoppers have most recently scooped up in droves in the list below. 
 1. Amazon A micro-needling serum that reviewers call "witchcraft"
 When we first featured the VT Cosmetics Reedle Shot serum , it was because the reviewers who had tried it likened it to something like "witchcraft in a bottle" for its purported ability to simulate microneedling treatments at home. If you don't already know, microneedling is an expensive and slightly uncomfortable in-office procedure that can do wonders for hyperpigmentation, acne scarring, fine lines, and more.
 While not always a feasible option for most, this serum is a much more affordable alternative with the added benefit of Korean wild ginseng PDRN. According to the brand, this innovative formula uses a "micro-needling mechanism that promotes instant skin enhancement for a smoother, softer feel." This component also maximizes product absorption for better results and will impart a slight tingling feeling on the skin.
 Reedle Shot customers appear to be blown away by the results of this slightly odd-feeling serum that one person claims "drastically improved the texture of my skin," while another said , " I find this to feel more effective than microneedling."
 $24 at Amazon $26 at Ulta 2-pack: $26 at Olive Young 2. Amazon An arbutin cream that's actually fading hyperpigmentation
 Unlike your run-of-the-mill sun spots, we know that melasma is arguably one of the most clingy and temperamental skin conditions to treat. That's what makes this Korean drugstore cream — originally featured mid-last year and then again when we called it one of the most effective beauty products of 2025 before going on to award it a HuffPost Shopping award in April — all the more impressive. 
 It contains a 7% concentration of arbutin , an antioxidant with brightening properties that works by inhibiting the over-production of melanin in the skin, which causes hyperpigmentation. It contains other well-trusted ingredients in the world of melasma care, one of which is 4% tranexamic acid , which is revered for its ability to reduce pigmentation associated with melasma, without causing any kind of irritation.
 There’s also niacinamide , a workhorse antioxidant that you’re most likely already familiar with. If you’re not, just know that this all-skin-concerns ingredient can reduce redness, acne, and, most notably, brighten the complexion.
 $25 at Amazon 3. Amazon A collagen-packed multi-balm for staving off crow's feet, marionette lines and more
 The Dr. Melaxin Calcium Multi-Balm has been a recurring top seller since the first time our Daily Sales team first reported on its age-defying potential, in the words of reviewers. This versatile stick, which is being called “ a time machine for my face ,” and “ PERFECTION in a stick ,” is a fast-absorbing oil-balm that can be swiped under and around the eyes, the forehead, or any other areas of concern.
 Aimed at smoothing fine lines and surface dehydration, the formula contains calcium, vitamin D, collagen and other powerhouse ingredients such as adenosine for firming and boosted skin elasticity. 
 $19 at Amazon $19 at Target $23 at YesStyle Advertisement 
 4. Amazon A juicy "miracle cream" bursting with hyaluronic acid and PDRN for impactful hydration
 Our first impression of this Korean PDRN cream by Anua was when one reviewer compared it to "a miracle cream" and said they were unable to say enough good things about this under-$25 formula. It then went on to receive a HuffPost Shopping award in April after readers appeared to enthusiastically agree.
 PDRN, as it's been previously described to us by board-certified dermatologists, is a portion of DNA that’s typically derived from salmon sperm and has been shown to accelerate repair of damaged skin and promote new tissue growth. It also boosts hydration in the skin, promotes cellular turnover and reduces hyperpigmentation.
 The cream also offers other anti-aging heavy-hitters, like hyaluronic acid for plumping and hydration, niacinamide for protection, squalane for softening, glycerin for moisture, and turmeric, aloe and eggplant extras for soothing and brightening. Lightweight and non-greasy, users say it quickly soaks into your skin and plays well with other products.
 One 40-year-old reviewer , with combination dry and oily skin and ance, says after using the cream, “I have elasticity and softness as I had in my 20s.” They also note that they’ve been getting many compliments on their skin — something they are not used to. “My face at 65 years old looks and feels about 40,” another wrote. 
 $24 at Amazon $24 at Ulta $20 at Yes Style 5. Amazon A "bounce balm" that you can swipe on your skin for instant hydration 
 Another PDRN-filled product that has managed to earn a HuffPost Shopping award is this reader-favorite multi-balm that makes smoothing and hydrating the trouble areas on your face, impossibly easy. 
 Featured in the fall , the Kahi Wrinkle Bounce balm is a lightweight and hydrating stick, enriched with fermented jeju oil and a collagen combo with salmon DNA (the PDRN portion of this formula), which works to deeply moisturize the skin and support skin renewal. Additionally, the balm helps diminish fine lines and improve skin clarity to reveal a more radiant complexion. 
 HuffPost readers and Kahi Balm reviewers alike have had a longstanding obsession with this treatment stick, which you can swipe under the eyes to target dehydration and crow's feet, on the lips and forehead.
 "I just turned 50. I have always taken care of my skin and looked younger than my age, but this year I started to notice more wrinkles popping up," one Amazon shopper wrote , " I started using this every night before bed, all around my eyes and lips. After about a week, I saw a huge difference!"
 $23 at Amazon $16.25 at Ulta (Regularly $25) $25 at iHerb 6. Amazon The "your-skin-but-better" color correcting cream
 Whether you’re struggling with a condition like rosacea or are simply prone to irritation, there’s one item that doubles as both skin care and makeup with legions of devoted fans (both online and in the HuffPost newsroom ) that is formulated to correct even the ruddiest complexion, and it is worth every penny. 
 According to many, the Erborian CC Red Correct color-correcting cream is one of the best K-beauty products out there. It's designed to help neutralize redness and calm skin in both the short and long term, with more visible benefits the longer you use it. It also has SPF 25 sun protection. It's formulated with centella asiatica, also known as tiger grass, which has been used for thousands of years for its soothing and calming properties . The inclusion of glycerin can hydrate and strengthen the skin's natural moisture barrier, so your skin stays soft and supple even while the active ingredients work hard to nourish the skin. 
 The critical mass of positive testimony from our colleagues here at HuffPost made it a no-brainer when it came to including it in this year's HuffPost Shopping awards . HuffPost senior reporter Lydia O’Connor called it “a miracle product.” She came across it while searching for something to counter her skin’s redness and blotchiness, saying, "It’s very your-skin-but-better and just sort of blurs everything while cutting down on red undertones.” She uses it by itself on her “no makeup days” but finds that it’s great under foundation and concealer as well.
 HuffPost senior reporter Carly Ledbetter said, “As someone with rosacea, it is the only ‘green’ product that makes my skin look normal.” Senior reporter Jessica Schulberg chimed in, saying, “I’ve influenced every single one of my friends to try it, it’s literally the only makeup I wear now. It’s magical.” 
 The finish is lighter than I expected from such a transformative product, so even those with dry skin or who are acne-prone can enjoy it. It is also worth noting that this product is best suited for those with lighter skin tones who are prone to redness. Those with more melanated skin may find that it leaves a white cast.
 $26+ at Amazon $26+ at Sephora $26+ at Dermstore Advertisement 
 7. Amazon Exfoliating pore pads packed with lactic and salicylic acids
 The Medicube Zero Pore pads are a favorite of senior shopping writer and beauty-obsessive Lourdes Avila Uribe, who said : "I’ve ditched my traditional AHA serums for these bad boys, and my skin has never looked better."
 Featured across several HuffPost stories and one of the recipients of this year's HuffPost Shopping awards , the Medicube pads are designed to help exfoliate, balance and brighten skin, reducing oil production, minimizing breakouts and refining the look of pores. They are formulated with powerful alpha and beta hydroxy acids like white willow bark, vitamin C and calming botanical extracts like lavender to soothe. We also find them to be a great alternative to some of the pricier exfoliation pads that HuffPost readers also seem to adore. 
 $19 at Amazon $21 at Target $21 at iHerb 8. Amazon A jelly lip mask that smoothes lip lines
 At the beginning of March this year, I reported on my experience with the Abib PDRN collagen lip jelly mask , a delightfully hydrating glaze that I bought in the hopes that it would minimize the appearance of my lip lines, make my pout look more plump and, above all, stave off my chronic dryness — especially around the corners of my mouth where regular retinol use can make it go flaky.
 I was bolstered in my buying decision after seeing many users claiming that this thick and nourishing lip gel “was the best product” they had ever used and worked miraculously on wrinkled, aging lips .
 When I tried it for myself, I found it instantly moisturizing and soothing, and now, after regular use, my lips are less dry in general and much smoother-looking, even when I didn’t have any lip product on. My lips also look more flattering under matte lipstick formulas because my dryness-related lines are less defined. Not quite a balm and not quite a gloss, but somewhere in a delightful jammy middle, the Abib treatment contains PDRN (a K-beauty ingredient that we've done extensive reporting on), collagen amino acids and hyaluronic acid, a popular humectant that draws moisture in and acts as a barrier to prevent hydration loss.
 $12+ at Amazon $16 at iHerb 9. Amazon A milky PDRN toner that hydrates like no other
 One of the top-selling products from a HuffPost story in March that contained several of HuffPost's editors' most beloved beauty products was the Medicube PDRN milky toner , an ultra-hydrating skin glaze that I have purchased again and again. 
 I pat it into my skin after washing my face and before applying any serums or creams to prep my skin for optimal absorption and long-lasting moisture. It's thicker than your average toner or essence and doubly hydrating, packed with salmon-derived PDRN to boost collagen production and ceramides to strengthen the skin barrier —an absolute must for someone with dry, sensitive skin. This formula also contains peptides for more plumping action and niacinamide, which I trust to give me a more radiant complexion and fade dark spots.
 $18 at Amazon $21 at Nordstrom $21 at Ulta Advertisement 
 10. Amazon Round Lab's Moisturizing Birch Juice sunscreen that feels invisible 
 Another crowd-pleasing product that proved itself to be a HuffPost reader favorite this year is the Round Lab Moisturizing Birch Juice sunscreen , a formula that's sure to defy whatever notions you might have previously felt about sunscreens.
 Like many Korean sunscreen formulations, this daily sun cream is lightweight, non-greasy and fast-absorbing and doesn't leave a white cast. The broad-spectrum SPF 50 formula feels cool and refreshing on the skin and contains both birch tree sap and hyaluronic acid to help keep skin moisturized throughout the day.
 Though featured back in 2023 , Uribe recently reiterated her love of the formula by saying that she's been using it all winter long and the dry, cold weather has been no match for this lush formulation. "It has a really beautiful finish that leaves my skin glowing and is a great primer for makeup. It's a great daily SPF that works with a range of skin tones and is hydrating without clogging pores or feeling slimy. It's one of my favorite K-beauty sunscreens," she said.
 $22+ at Amazon $25 at Target $25 at Ulta 11. Amazon A rosemary and PDRN hair system for thicker tresses 
 Medicube is a K-beauty name well-known for its skin care, so when the brand launched a hair care line earlier this year, I was eager to report on it . It's safe to say that HuffPost readers appeared to respond with equal excitement. 
 This three-product system combines ingredients and delivery methods popular in K-beauty skin care and applies them to the scalp, with the intent of making hair appear fuller and creating optimal conditions to encourage hair growth. All products in the line feature rosemary extract, an ingredient that board-certified dermatologists have previously told us not only conditions and strengthens hair, but also helps reduce damage and breakage, thereby contributing to a stronger hair appearance.
 The products also include PDRN , an ingredient you would normally find in just skin care, but as it applies to hair care, the brand claims PDRN can help promote a healthier scalp that, in turn, produces healthier hair from the root. Although we haven’t gotten direct confirmation of this claim from experts, some studies point to PDRN as an effective way to stimulate hair follicles and reduce inflammation when injected into the scalp.
 Though relatively new to market, Medicube users assure us that it has helped to make hair appear fuller almost instantly and has even helped with conditions like scalp psoriasis , which can inhibit hair growth.
 $55 at Amazon 12. Amazon An ultra-calming recovery cream that strengthens the skin barrier
 Back in March , HuffPost freelance writer Vivian Chung reported on Dr. Althea 345 Relief cream , a recently viral K-beauty moisturizer praised for calming redness, irritation and dehydration, with some users saying it works after just one use. 
 "With the goal to calm the redness that comes with my hormonal acne and eczema-prone skin, especially during the colder winter months, I decided to give it a try for the next two months," Chung wrote. "Almost instantly, my itchy patches felt smoother and far less tempting to scratch, and after consistently applying it morning and evening, I noticed that it helped soothe the redness on my cheeks and chin while keeping my oily skin comfortably hydrated."
 She explained that the formula centers on tea tree leaf water, its primary active ingredient, to help calm visible redness and irritation while offering mild antibacterial support — a win for acne-prone complexions. Additionally, this multi-layered cream is enriched with ceramides for barrier repair and niacinamide for helping to fade dark spots and hyperpigmentation. 
 $27 at Amazon $27 at Ulta Advertisement 
 13. Amazon A caviar PDRN sheet mask from Biodance
 HuffPost contributor Claire Gallam recently tested her way through some of the most popular Korean face masks currently out there and reported that the Biodance Rejuvenating Caviar PDRN masks were among her top favorites, and HuffPost readers wanted to try them out for themselves. 
 These jelly sheet masks boast a concentrated dose of PDRN, with ultra-low molecular collagen so the particles can absorb and appear to tighten pores quicker than others. 
 "My nose, which is always a point of contention for me, had visibly reduced pores in both real life and photos after just one use. Plus, it brightened my skin instantly too, giving me that fresh-from-the-sauna glow," Gallam reported.
 $19 at Amazon $19 at Sephora Related
